newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche to leave supervisory board chairs.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche to leave supervisory board chairs.

text.p: Rolf Breuer, the new chief executive at Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, said that top Deutsche Bank executives would gradually withdraw from the chairmanship of supervisory boards in other countries.

Breuer, speaking to journalists for the first time since he took office on May 20, called on the Bonn parliament to cut back the maximum number of supervisory board members per company to 12 from 20 currently.

"The main opposition to such a move comes from the unions," Breuer said. "Although you have to ask yourself whether 10 union representatives can achieve more than six...But industry and the banks are in favour."

Financial problems at some German companies which have apparently gone unnoticed by the supervisory board have led to complaints that supervisory board members have too many responsibilities as they are on too many boards.

Parallel to that runs a discussion about the power of banks within the German economy. Germany's house bank system and the high level of cross shareholding in the economy means that many bank representatives have seats on other companies' boards.
Breuer added that a cut in the number of supervisory board members would automatically lead to a reconsideration of exactly who should take a supervisory board post.

"We would have to look at specific skills, the time available, individual's qualifications...without putting too fine a point on it, this could lead to a reduction in the number of bank representatives," he said.
Breuer rejected the idea that Deutsche Bank should set the pace for others by abandoning all of its supervisory board mandates.
"There are times when you have to leave some things to the lawmaker," he said.
